ex_officio.label: Holds it by virtue of another post

nodes.title: Voters
nodes.description: Every citizen aged 18 or over who is on the electoral roll (Art. 326). The start of every chain on this site.

nodes.title: Lok Sabha
nodes.description: House of the People. 543 members elected from single-member constituencies.

nodes.title: Rajya Sabha

selection.note: Elected by the elected MLAs of each state (single transferable vote); 12 members nominated by the President.

nodes.term: Permanent house; members serve 6 years, a third retiring every 2 years

nodes.title: Electoral college for President
nodes.description: Elected members of both Houses of Parliament and of the Legislative Assemblies of the states, Delhi and Puducherry.

nodes.title: Electoral college for Vice-President
nodes.description: All members of both Houses of Parliament, including nominated members.

nodes.title: Union Council of Ministers
nodes.description: Collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. The body that actually advises the President.

nodes.title: Appointments Committee of the Cabinet

selection.basis: Government of India (Transaction of Business) Rules

nodes.description: Approves senior appointments in the Union government: secretaries, heads of agencies, service chiefs, directors of many institutions.

nodes.title: Supreme Court collegium

selection.basis: Second and Third Judges Cases (1993, 1998); Memorandum of Procedure

nodes.description: The Chief Justice of India and the four senior-most Supreme Court judges. Recommends appointments to the Supreme Court and High Courts; the government can return a name once.

nodes.title: Selection committee for Election Commissioners

selection.basis: Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023, s. 7

nodes.description: The Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha (or leader of the largest opposition party), and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister.

nodes.title: Selection committee for CBI Director

selection.basis: Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946, s. 4A

nodes.description: The Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition (or leader of the largest opposition party) in the Lok Sabha, and the Chief Justice of India or a Supreme Court judge nominated by them.

nodes.title: Selection committee for Central Vigilance Commission
Selection committee for Central Information Commission

selection.note: Also includes an eminent jurist nominated by the other members.

selection.basis: Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, s. 4

selection.note: Chaired by the Central Vigilance Commissioner, with the Vigilance Commissioners and the Home, Personnel and Revenue Secretaries.

nodes.title: Financial Sector Regulatory Appointments Search Committee

selection.note: Chaired by the Cabinet Secretary with the Finance Ministry secretaries and outside experts. Shortlists candidates for RBI, SEBI and other regulators; the ACC decides.

nodes.title: Union Public Service Commission
nodes.description: Runs the Civil Services Examination that recruits IAS, IPS and other all-India officers, and empanels officers for posts such as state police chief.

nodes.title: GST Council
nodes.description: The Union Finance Minister (chair) and the finance ministers of every state. Sets GST rates for the whole country.

nodes.title: President of India
nodes.description: Head of state. Acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers (Art. 74). Formally appoints most of the officers listed here.

nodes.title: Vice-President of India
nodes.description: Ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
nodes.removal: Resolution of the Rajya Sabha agreed to by the Lok Sabha (Art. 67(b))

nodes.title: Prime Minister
nodes.description: The President appoints the person who can command a majority in the Lok Sabha.
nodes.term: Holds office while commanding a majority in the Lok Sabha

nodes.title: Union Home Minister
nodes.description: Oversees the central police organisations, intelligence and internal security.

nodes.title: Union Health and Family Welfare Minister
Cabinet Secretary
nodes.description: Senior-most civil servant; heads the civil service and chairs the Committee of Secretaries.

nodes.title: Attorney General for India
nodes.term: At the pleasure of the President

selection.basis: Salary and Allowances of Leaders of Opposition in Parliament Act, 1977
selection.note: Recognised by the Speaker; by convention the leader of the largest opposition party with at least a tenth of the seats.

selection.basis: Salary and Allowances of Leaders of Opposition in Parliament Act, 1977

nodes.title: Chief Justice of India

selection.note: By convention the senior-most Supreme Court judge, named by the outgoing Chief Justice.

nodes.removal: Address by both Houses of Parliament on proven misbehaviour or incapacity (Art. 124(4))

nodes.title: Judges of the Supreme Court
nodes.removal: Address by both Houses of Parliament (Art. 124(4))

nodes.title: Comptroller and Auditor General
nodes.description: Audits the accounts of the Union and state governments.

selection.basis: Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, s. 4
selection.note: Must be a former Chief Justice of India or Supreme Court judge.

nodes.title: Chairman, Finance Commission
nodes.description: Constituted every five years to recommend how tax revenue is divided between the Union and the states.

nodes.title: Chairman, Securities and Exchange Board of India

selection.note: Chosen from a search-cum-selection committee panel.
The President, as Visitor, picks from a panel prepared by a search-cum-selection committee.
Appointed by the Visitor (the President) on a search-cum-selection committee's recommendation.
Chosen on the recommendation of a search committee chaired by the Cabinet Secretary.
A third elected by MLAs, a third by local bodies, a twelfth each by graduates and teachers, and a sixth nominated by the Governor.

nodes.title: State Council of Ministers
nodes.description: The 'state government' that posts district officers and runs departments.

nodes.title: High Court
nodes.description: Several states share one High Court; see the state's details.

nodes.title: High Court collegium
nodes.description: The Chief Justice and two senior-most judges of the High Court. Initiates names for appointment as High Court judges.

nodes.title: Selection committee for State Information Commission
Selection committee for State Human Rights Commission

selection.basis: Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, s. 22

selection.note: Composition differs by state; this is the most common pattern.

nodes.title: Governor
nodes.description: Formal head of the state. Also chancellor of most state universities.
nodes.term: 5 years, at the pleasure of the President

selection.note: In Chandigarh the Governor of Punjab is Administrator ex officio.

nodes.title: Chief Minister
nodes.description: The Governor appoints the person who can command a majority in the Assembly.

selection.note: Often held by the Chief Minister.

nodes.title: Leader of Opposition in the Assembly
Chief Secretary

selection.note: An IAS officer chosen by the Chief Minister, usually from the senior-most batches.

nodes.description: Head of the state's civil service.

nodes.title: Chief Justice of the High Court

selection.note: By convention appointed from outside the state.
The High Court collegium proposes names; the state government comments; the Supreme Court collegium recommends; the President appoints.

nodes.title: Director General of Police

selection.basis: Prakash Singh v. Union of India (2006)
selection.note: The state picks from three officers empanelled by UPSC; minimum tenure of two years.

nodes.description: Head of the state police force.

nodes.title: State Election Commissioner
nodes.description: Runs panchayat and municipal elections (the Election Commission of India runs Assembly and Lok Sabha elections).
nodes.removal: Only like a High Court judge

nodes.title: Chairman, State Public Service Commission
nodes.description: Recruits state civil servants, including many judicial magistrates.

nodes.title: State Finance Commission
nodes.description: Recommends how state revenue is shared with panchayats and municipalities.

nodes.title: Labour Commissioner
nodes.description: Enforces labour law and minimum wages in the state.

nodes.title: Inspector General of Registration and Stamps
nodes.description: Runs property registration and stamp duty collection.

selection.note: Selection committee headed by the High Court Chief Justice or a judge they nominate.
In most states the Governor, as Chancellor, appoints from a search committee's panel. Several states have legislated or litigated to change this.

nodes.title: District Magistrate

selection.note: Usually an IAS officer (recruited through UPSC) posted and transferred by the state government.

nodes.description: Chief administrator of the district: revenue, law and order, disaster response, elections.

selection.basis: Representation of the People Act, 1950, s. 13AA
selection.note: The District Magistrate, designated by the Election Commission.
Usually an IPS officer. Cities with a police commissionerate have a Commissioner of Police instead.
Promoted from the subordinate judiciary or recruited directly from advocates with 7 years' practice.
Recruited by examination; the High Court controls postings and discipline.
Chosen from a panel the District Magistrate prepares in consultation with the Sessions Judge.

nodes.title: District Legal Services Authority
nodes.description: Free legal aid and Lok Adalats. Chaired by the District Judge.

selection.note: Lok Sabha constituencies do not follow district lines; this lists MPs whose constituency covers part of the district.

nodes.title: Chief Medical Officer
nodes.description: Runs government hospitals, health centres and disease programmes in the district.

selection.note: Appointed by the public sector bank that RBI designates as the district's lead bank.

nodes.title: District Registrar / Sub-Registrars
nodes.description: Registers property sales and collects stamp duty.

nodes.title: Tehsildar
nodes.description: Keeps land records, issues certificates, collects land revenue.

nodes.title: Patwari
nodes.description: Village-level keeper of land records.

nodes.title: Gram Sabha
nodes.description: Every registered voter in a village. Approves plans and beneficiary lists.

selection.note: Most states elect the sarpanch directly; some have them chosen by elected ward members.
Varies by state: directly elected in some (for example Uttar Pradesh), chosen by councillors in others (for example Maharashtra and Delhi).

nodes.title: Municipal Commissioner
nodes.description: Runs the municipal administration day to day.

nodes.title: Station House Officer
nodes.description: Officer in charge of a police station; registers FIRs.

nodes.title: Member of Lok Sabha

selection.basis: Art. 81; Representation of the People Act, 1951

nodes.description: One member is elected from each territorial Lok Sabha constituency.

selection.note: Elected members of each State Legislative Assembly choose the state's representatives by proportional representation using the single transferable vote; the President nominates 12 additional members.

nodes.title: Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA)

selection.basis: Art. 170; Representation of the People Act, 1951

nodes.description: One member is elected from each Vidhan Sabha constituency.

nodes.title: Indian Administrative Service

selection.basis: All India Services Act, 1951; IAS Cadre Rules, 1954

nodes.description: An All India Service with officers allocated to state cadres and also deputed to the Union.

nodes.title: Indian Police Service

selection.basis: All India Services Act, 1951; IPS Cadre Rules, 1954

nodes.description: An All India Service whose officers lead police organisations at Union, state, commissionerate and district levels.

nodes.title: Indian Forest Service

selection.basis: All India Services Act, 1951; Indian Forest Service Cadre Rules, 1966

nodes.description: An All India Service that staffs forest departments and conservation administration. Often abbreviated IFoS to distinguish it from the Foreign Service.

nodes.title: Indian Foreign Service
nodes.description: The central civil service that staffs India's diplomatic missions and the Ministry of External Affairs.

selection.note: The licensee may be a state-owned distribution company, municipal undertaking, cooperative, or private concessionaire. A private operator is selected under state procurement or a concession/privatisation process, not elected by residents; the state electricity regulatory commission licenses it and sets tariffs.

Responsibility varies among a municipality, parastatal water board, development authority, or a competitively procured private operator. Residents elect municipal councillors, but do not elect a private concessionaire.

selection.basis: State municipal Acts and pollution-control law
selection.note: Usually a municipal body or water/sewerage board; construction or operation can be tendered to a private contractor or public-private concessionaire under the applicable procurement rules.

selection.basis: Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016; state municipal law
selection.note: The municipality remains accountable even where collection, transport, processing, or disposal is awarded through a tender or concession. The provider is selected through procurement, not elected.
